sections.voiceover: On November 12, 2026, the European Space Agency released the DR1-Foundation dataset from Euclid. How vast is this sky map?
sections.visual_cue: High-resolution sky map overlay highlighting a sweeping patch of 1,900 square degrees across celestial coordinates.
sections.sfx_cue: Digital data scanning chimes and soft ambient swell.
b_roll: ESA official sky map release visualization of DR1-Foundation
Euclid space telescope assembly in cleanroom
sections.transition_out: Cross-dissolve into moon grid comparison graphic

sections.voiceover: But that Euclid survey isn't small, covering an expanse equal to 9,500 full Moons.
sections.visual_cue: Scale graphic comparing the surveyed sky swath against thousands of full Moon disk shapes.
b_roll: Night sky illustration with repeating Moon grid overlay
sections.transition_out: Sharp flash cut to percentage survey gauge

sections.voiceover: The Euclid Consortium confirmed this represents only 14% of the planned 6-year area. Observations from spring 2024 to spring 2025 created this dataset.
sections.visual_cue: 3D universe map grid expanding to demonstrate 14 percent coverage against the 6-year sky plan.
sections.sfx_cue: Expansive orchestral brass swell and electronic pulse.
b_roll: 3D universe point cloud rendering from scientific dataset
Euclid focal plane sensor optical beam simulation
sections.transition_out: Slow dissolve into wide starry expanse

sections.voiceover: Fourteen percent of the mission revealed 1 billion objects.
sections.visual_cue: Dramatic static lockoff of deep space with subtle particle shimmer.
